doc.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

title: Latest CD and sign-off
summary: Banter about the Hindenberg title, how quickly he records, the mother's quote title, and thanks.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Some good thoughts. And I’m going to have to go listen to you tonight and see if that happens.
Well that whole thing will come crashing apart. It will be like the Hindenberg.
I don’t know, I see, maybe the next CD, maybe there’s a title there for you, “The Hindenberg” or something. But I’m not sure, is this your latest?
I’ve done several since then. I turn them out like kielbasas you know, I mean, because in England and Germany they want something new. “Anything new?” “Anything?” “Oh, gosh, we got that one.”
But “Songs I Learned at my Mother’s Knee and Other Low Joints” is the title that we started off with, and your mother’s comment, which is really memorable. So thanks again for your time.
